snippet.title: Apex: How Charlize Theron’s Climb Shocked the Whole Crew | Collider BTS
snippet.description:
Director Baltasar Kormákur and cinematographer Lawrence Sher break down how Apex pushed Charlize Theron—and the entire crew—to their limits in some of the most unforgiving environments imaginable.

In this behind-the-scenes Apex interview, Kormákur and Sher explain how they shot deep in remote canyons and rivers, often hiking and swimming just to reach locations. The goal was total authenticity, creating a survival story where the landscape feels as dangerous as any antagonist. They reveal how the Blue Mountains’ unique geography created a mix of claustrophobia and scale that shaped the film’s visual language.

One of the standout moments? Charlize Theron going far beyond what was planned—turning a simple 10-foot climb into a full 30-foot ascent in a single take. “If I don’t hear cut, I’m going to keep going,” became a defining mindset for her performance.

The conversation also dives into how the team scaled down equipment, used drones for dynamic movement, and embraced unpredictable weather to enhance realism. It’s a rare look at how Apex blends large-scale filmmaking with a stripped-down, immersive approach.

snippet.title: Michael Craft Breakdown: The Art of Recreating Michael Jackson
snippet.description:
Costume designer Marci Rodgers breaks down the meticulous process behind bringing Michael Jackson’s legendary style to life in Antoine Fuqua’s Michael, revealing how Jaafar Jackson’s transformation became almost uncanny on set.

In this exclusive Michael movie interview, Rodgers walks through her 800-page research process, from studying rare archival photos to visiting museums and measuring original garments. She explains how every era—from the Jackson 5 to Thriller and beyond—required a distinct approach rooted in historical accuracy while still working for modern filmmaking.

Rodgers also shares how she balanced performance costumes with a more intimate look at “private Michael,” ensuring the film reflects both the global icon and the person behind it. One of the most fascinating reveals involves recreating the Grammy jacket, where a close inspection proved it was made with bugle beads—not sequins—changing the entire design process.

She also details how costumes were subtly engineered to support Jaafar Jackson’s dance movements, helping him fully embody Michael. In some moments, Rodgers says, the transformation was so convincing she found herself thinking, “That’s not Jaafar—that’s Michael.”

They discuss the creative process behind aging costumes, designing for stunt-heavy scenes, and how wardrobe subtly tracks Xavier’s emotional and physical transformation across Season 2.

The conversation also dives into standout influences—from Elvis-inspired pieces to Western imagery—and why one specific shot of Xavier on horseback became so meaningful. Brown shares stories from set, including filming in mud-soaked wardrobe and intentionally embracing discomfort to enhance performance.

Coxy highlights the collaborative nature of costume design on a large-scale production, working closely with stunts, production design, and directors to ensure every detail feels authentic. Together, they offer a thoughtful look at how costume becomes a “second skin” for the character—and a key storytelling device in Paradise.
